{{Quote|I believe it's a fragment of hull plating that crashed onto this moon from the battle station that got destroyed in this vicinity last year. Very interesting technology, I must say.|Sergeant Ruwan Tokai|<ref name="SWG" />}}
'''Ruwan Tokai''' was a [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Tech Sergeant|technical sergeant]] of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] who was posted to the [[Great Temple/Legends|Great Temple]] of the [[Massassi/Legends|Massassi]] on [[Yavin 4/Legends|Yavin 4]] during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]]. A [[Standard year/Legends|year]] after the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]] in [[1 ABY/Legends|1 ABY]], [[Sergeant/Legends|Sergeant]] Tokai examined a piece of the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|DS-1 Orbital Battle Station]], a [[Moon/Legends|moon-sized]] Imperial [[Battle station/Legends|battle station]] better known as the [[Death Star/Legends|Death Star]]. After sending a [[Courier/Legends|courier]] of his to deliver the fragment to a [[Warrant Officer/Legends|warrant officer]] for further analysis, Sergeant Tokai was put at risk of [[Court-martial/Legends|court-martial]] due to the Death Star salvage being above his security clearance. To avoid punitive action, Sergeant Tokai procured from his superior [[Imperial officer/Legends|officer]] a "retroactive authorization" which retroactively granted the sergeant the right to have examined the piece of the massive Imperial battlestation.

==Biography==
{{Quote|Please, you have to help! That piece of the Death Star turned out to be classified above my clearance. I'm up for court martial, just for examining it! You have to get to my commanding officer and get a retroactive authorization.|Sergeant Ruwan Tokai to his courier|<ref name="SWG" />}}
A [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Tech Sergeant|technical sergeant]] of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] by the name of Ruwan Tokai was alive during [[Time/Legends|time]] of the major [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] conflict known as the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]],<ref name="SWG" /> during which the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]] won a decisive victory against the Galactic Empire at the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]] in [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]].<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> About [[0 ABY/Legends|6]] [[Standard month/Legends|months]] later, the Rebel Alliance [[Evacuation of Yavin|evacuated]] the [[Moon/Legends|moon]] of [[Yavin 4/Legends|Yavin 4]].<ref name="Doom Mission">"[[Doom Mission]]"</ref> By around [[1 ABY/Legends|1 ABY]], [[Sergeant/Legends|Sergeant]] Ruwan Tokai and other [[Imperial officer/Legends|Imperial officers]] were posted to the [[Great Temple/Legends|Great Temple]] of the [[Massassi/Legends|Massassi]] formerly used by the Rebel's as their base of operations.<ref name="SWG" />

During his time at the temple, Sergeant Tokai examined a fallen piece from the destroyed<ref name="SWG" /> [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|DS-1 Orbital Battle Station]], the [[Moon/Legends|moon-sized]] Imperial [[Battle station/Legends|battle station]] better known as the [[Death Star/Legends|Death Star]].<ref name="RECG">''[[Rebellion Era Campaign Guide]]''</ref> The Death Star fragment was an unidentifiable piece of [[Durasteel/Legends|durasteel]], possibly a [[Hull/Legends|hull]] fragment from the destroyed battlestation. While examining the piece, the sergeant lamented the affect the humidity of Yavin 4's [[Jungle/Legends|jungle]] environment had on their equipment. The Death Star fragment, for instance, was covered in [[Moss/Legends|moss]]. However, any attempt to clean the piece risked removing vital chemical traces which would help the Imperials learn what happened to the Death Star.<ref name="SWG" />
{{GameMechanics|legends=1|Star Wars Galaxies}}
To better examine the piece, Sergeant Ruwan Tokai sent a [[Courier/Legends|courier]] of his to deliver the fragment to a [[Warrant Officer/Legends|warrant officer II]] for further analysis. After the courier handed the fragment over to the warrant [[Officer/Legends|officer]] in the nearby [[Ersham Ridge]] region, the officer expressed surprise that the technical sergeant was allowed to examine it in the first place. All salvage from the Death Star was declared by the Empire as a classified secret. Arousing suspicion, the warrant officer said he would look into Sergeant Ruwan Tokai's clearance level. The courier returned to Sergeant Tokai to inform him of the warrant officer's suspicions, as well as to collect [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|payment]] allocated from Sergeant Tokai's equipment restoration budget. The technical sergeant claimed that no one had told him Death Star salvage was classified, and he hoped nothing bad would happen to him as a result of this fact.<ref name="SWG" />

Unfortunately for Ruwan Tokai, his worst fears were realized when he received news that he was at risk of being [[Court-martial/Legends|court-martialed]] for examining the piece of the Death Star, which was above his security clearance. Fearing he could be sent to the [[Spice mines of Kessel/Legends|Spice Mines]] of [[Kessel/Legends|Kessel]], Sergeant Tokai frantically begged his courier to procure a "retroactive authorization" from his superior officer, a man who held the [[Military rank/Legends|rank]] of [[Lieutenant Colonel/Legends|lieutenant colonel]] in the [[Imperial Military/Legends|Imperial Military]]. The courier agreed to help out the panicked sergeant, even though this meant traversing a dangerous area of the Ersham Ridge known to harbor Rebel activity. Although the courier was attacked by a Rebel [[First Lieutenant/Legends|first lieutenant]] and two of their [[Alliance Special Forces/Legends|commandos]], the courier managed to [[Death/Legends|kill]] them off, and successfully reach Ruwan Tokai's superior officer. Fortunately for Sergeant Tokai, his superior was understanding of his situation, and dismissed it as an understandable little slip-up. With the retroactive authorization procured, the courier returned to a grateful Ruwan Tokai, who paid the loyal Imperial servant out of his own funds. Free to continue his service to the Empire, Sergeant Ruwan Tokai then remembered that the warrant officer had also examined the same Death Star piece. Tokai hoped that he would not get into the same kind of trouble as he did.<ref name="SWG" />
{{Endgame}}

==Personality and traits==
[[File:DeathStarFragment.png|70px|thumb|The small Death Star fragment examined by Technical Sergeant Ruwan Tokai]]
{{Quote|All salvage from the Death Star has been a classified secret. You say a technical sergeant sent this? Hmm. We'll have to look into his clearances.|An Imperial warrant officer II speaking about Sergean Ruwan Tokai|<ref name="SWG" />}}
Ruwan Tokai had fair skin, brown [[Hair/Legends|hair]], and [[Color/Legends|blue-colored]] [[Eye/Legends|eyes]]. During his time at the Great Temple, Ruwan Tokai remarked how he despised the humidity of the jungle moon. Nevertheless, he carried on his duties, sometimes with ill conceived consequences. When Sergeant Tokai was at risk of court-martial for examining a piece of the Death Star above his security clearance, the Imperial officer panicked, and begged his courier to retrieve a retroactive authorization from his superior. Ruwan Tokai had something of a generous disposition. When the courier carried out his tasks, he saw to it that the individual received compensation, either from his allocated budget, or from his very own personal funds.<ref name="SWG" />

==Equipment==
{{Quote|I despise the humidity on this world&mdash;so bad for the equipment. I need this piece taken to the warrant officer for analysis.|Sergeant Ruwan Tokai|<ref name="SWG" />}}
During his post at the Great Temple on Yavin 4, Ruwan Tokai wore a typical [[Imperial officer's uniform/Legends|Imperial officer's uniform]]. This [[Imperial military uniforms/Legends|uniform]] consisted of a grey [[Imperial officer's tunic/Legends|tunic]] and trousers, a [[Hat/Legends|cap]] with an affixed [[Officer's disk/Legends|officer's disc]], a black [[Belt/Legends|belt]] with a [[Silver/Legends|silver-colored]] buckle, black [[Boot/Legends|boots]], and black [[Officer's gloves|gloves]].<ref name="SWG" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|You didn't get me that authorization? Oh, no! How will I explain this. It's Kessel for me.|Sergeant Ruwan Tokai to players who failed to procure a retroactive authorization|<ref name="SWG" />}}
Sergeant Ruwan Tokai was a non-player character in the [[2003]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] [[Star Wars Galaxies|''Star Wars Galaxies: An Empire Divided'']], a [[Roleplaying game|massively multiplayer online role-playing game]] developed by [[Sony]] Online Entertainment and published by [[LucasArts]], prior to its closure on [[December 15]], [[2011]].<ref name="SWG" /><ref name="Shutdown">{{SonyCite|url=playerinfo|text=IMPORTANT INFORMATION ABOUT ''STAR WARS'' GALAXIES™}}</ref> Players who performed a series of [[W:c:swg:Quest|quests]] for Tokai had to deliver a [[W:c:swg:Death Star Fragment (Part 1)|Death Star fragment]] to a warrant officer, and receive a [[W:c:swg:Death Star Fragment (Part 2)|retroactive authorization]] from a lieutenant colonel. Completing the first quest would earn the player 40 [[W:c:swg:Imperial Credit|credits]], while completing the second would earn the player 50 credits. Although the player could choose not to do Tokai's quests, this article assumes 100% game completion. Ruwan Tokai was one of only few NPCs in [[W:c:swg:Star Wars Galaxies|''Star Wars Galaxies'']] for which a definitive quest timeline could be established. In his first quest, he referenced the destruction of the Death Star as having taken place "last year," indicating a quest timeline of around 1 ABY.<ref name="SWG" />
